subject: Unexpected 429s — ratecap ledger mismatch and immediate remediation
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.n@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-01T08:14:22Z
Subject: Unexpected 429s — temporary override and next steps

Hi Sarah,

Thank you for the flag earlier today — I wanted to reach out with an immediate update and plan. Our telemetry shows HelioHealth experienced an uptick in 429 (Rate Limit) responses between 07:50–08:05 UTC this morning. The root cause appears to be a configuration mismatch between the tenant-level rate ledger and the org-level quota mapping: a translation script incorrectly applied an older tenant quota to your production org, resulting in bursts that exceeded the active enforcement window.

What we did right away:
- Applied an emergency tenant override for HelioHealth (tenanted burst window widened) to eliminate user-facing 429s while we investigate.
- Isolated the offending translation job in the deployment pipeline and paused the next scheduled run.
- Captured detailed logs and a ledger dump (attached: ratecap-ledger-dump-0901.csv) for your team and our ops investigation.

Immediate impact and mitigation:
- We estimate ~2,300 API calls returned 429 during the spike (most were short-lived, <90s).
- No customer content was dropped — requests were throttled, not replayed.
- We have a timeline for a full remediation plan and a postmortem draft; I’ll share the draft for your review tomorrow.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm you'd like us to issue a one-time usage credit for the throttled requests (we can pre-authorize in parallel with the postmortem).
2) Walkthrough of the attached ledger and logs with your engineering team — can we schedule a 30-min slot today or tomorrow?
3) We will roll a permanent guardrail to prevent this translation script from applying legacy quotas to active production orgs.

I’m very sorry for the disruption. Marcus and Lauren are looped here to confirm technical details and timeline.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ratecap-ledger-dump-0901.csv (CSV), logs_summary.txt (text)

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the quick response and the override. A few quick Qs from our side: 

- Can you confirm which environments and API keys were affected? We need to check our dashboards and inform CS/ops.
- We’d like confirmation on the credit — HelioHealth prefers a one-time usage credit rather than retroactive invoice adjustments. Can you confirm the process and ETA?
- For the postmortem, can your team include a short summary of the changes you’ll put in place and an estimated timeline for the guardrail?

Hugh is our SRE lead (cc’d) and can join a tech walkthrough this afternoon if you have availability.

Best,
Sarah
Head of Product, HelioHealth

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-09-01T11:18:47Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s — temporary override and next steps

Kim,

Quick technical notes for the record and for Sarah/Hugh if helpful in the walkthrough:

Root cause summary (ops):
- A background translation job intended to map legacy tenant quotas to v2 quota ledger used an outdated mapping table (v2_map_2025.csv) due to a deploy-time artifact. The job applied a mapping to HelioHealth that reduced their effective burst allowance for the enforcement window starting 07:45 UTC.
- Enforcement engine enforced the ledger atomically (correctly) — the failure is the wrong ledger value being applied.

Remediation actions completed: 
- Emergency override applied at 08:00 UTC (removed enforcement for the tenant-level burst window for 30 minutes while we validated).
- Translation job paused and artifact removed from the scheduled pipeline.
- We recreated the correct ledger mapping and pushed to a canary cluster for validation.

Planned follow-ups (owners/timeline):
- Marcus: Complete canary validation and roll the corrected translation mapping to production in 24h (ETA 2026-09-02 12:00 UTC).
- Lauren: Implement an automated alert that detects ledger mapping divergences and posts to Ops channel (ETA 72h).
- Kimberly: Coordinate customer communication and credit confirmation with Sarah/procurement (ETA 24–48h).

Notes on customer impact and credits:
- I estimate the throttled calls equate to ~350k tokens total. If we grant a one-time credit, finance will translate that into a dollar amount; we should confirm HelioHealth's preference for credit vs invoice adj.

Marcus
Principal Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.n@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, procurement@heliohealth.com
Date: 2026-09-02T16:02:11Z
Subject: Post-incident summary and proposed credit — HelioHealth

Hi Sarah / Hugh / procurement team,

Thanks again for your patience while our engineering team completed the validation and roll. This note summarizes the event, actions taken, and the proposal for remediation and credit. Please let me know if you'd like expanded details or a joint review call.

Event summary:
- Window: 2026-09-01 07:50–08:05 UTC.
- Cause: translation job applied legacy quota mapping to HelioHealth tenant (configuration/artefact mismatch).
- Customer-visible effect: ~2,300 API requests returned 429s; median disruption per request < 90s; no data loss.

Actions completed:
- Emergency tenant override applied (08:00 UTC).
- Stopped and removed the translation job artifact (08:30 UTC).
- Corrected ledger mapping validated in canary and rolled to prod (completed 2026-09-02 12:00 UTC).
- Added temporary monitoring: ledger divergence alert to Ops (will be automated by Lauren).

Proposed remediation/compensation:
- One-time usage credit to be applied to the next billing cycle covering the throttled calls (finance will calculate based on token estimate).
- A joint technical postmortem draft (attached: postmortem-draft-HelioHealth-0902.md) for your review; we'll finalize after any feedback.
- Timeline for guardrail automation: initial alerting in 72h, full CI deploy-time validation in 14 days.

Next steps for us:
1) I’ll loop in Finance to draft the credit amount and share it by EOD 2026-09-03.
2) Marcus will share a short runbook for SREs to detect affected API keys and re-run quota reconciliation if you want to run a customer-side check.
3) If you want an async review of the postmortem draft, we’ll incorporate comments and publish a final copy next week.

If this plan looks good, Sarah, we’ll schedule the credit and a brief technical walkthrough.

Apologies again for the interruption — we take this very seriously and will work to prevent recurrence.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai

Attachments: postmortem-draft-HelioHealth-0902.md
